correctness.rationale: A primitive square-zero B over a length-k quotient has nonzero square-zero reduction, hence the image and kernel of the reduction are the same line. Choose v outside that line modulo the maximal ideal; (Bv,v) is a basis and exhibits B as a conjugate of the single Jordan block. Its stabilizer in GL_2 consists of equal unit diagonal entries and an arbitrary upper entry, giving (q−1)q^(2k−1). Reduction of GL_2 is surjective with q^(4k−4) lifts per invertible reduction, yielding P_k=(q²−1)q^(2k−2). For valuation c with 2c<n, multiplication by π^c identifies the matrix ideal with matrices over length n−c as sets; A²=0 is then exactly the condition on the primitive image over length n−2c, with q^(4c) lifts. The powers of q cancel the c-dependence. If 2c≥n all products vanish, so ideal-shell subtraction and the unique zero exhaust the rest. The high shells including zero contribute q^(4 floor(n/2)), and adding ceil(n/2) copies of the low count gives the stated total, including the field case q². For x=q²T, use Σ floor(n/2)x^n=x²/((1−x)^2(1+x)); the stated generating numerator 1−q²T² results. Direct entry-square enumeration independently verified Z/4, Z/8, Z/16, Z/9 and F_4[t]/(t²), with respective totals 28,112,640,153,496 and all valuation strata matching.
residual_risks: The proof is for matrix dimension two over commutative chain rings. Finite enumeration is not a general proof.

evidence: The older works identified bibliographically concern counts of nilpotent matrices over modular rings; their full texts could not be inspected. Theorem 2.6 in Danchev–García–Gómez Lozano is a potent-plus-square-zero decomposition theorem for finite commutative rings with square-zero Jacobson radical.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A count of all nilpotents cannot alone recover the square-zero subcount (diag(p,0) over Z/p³ is nilpotent but not square-zero). A decomposition existence theorem does not count square-zero summands, let alone their fine entry-valuation distribution. Older modular-case refinements remain unresolved, not excluded.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The module formulation does not change the labeled count. The exact dual-number count is a base-ring specialization of length two, not a result on all lengths; a trace constraint is not equivalent to square-zero over nonreduced rings.

value.rationale: Square-zero 2×2 matrices are a natural first nilpotency-index-bounded counting problem over nonreduced rings. The entry-valuation census separates constraints on primitive quotients from the automatic square-zero ideal range. The equal counts across genuinely different low strata, valid in mixed as well as equal characteristic and for every length, provide useful uniform local counting data beyond the already-known length-two slice or a total alone.
residual_risks: No count in larger matrix dimension or classification by conjugacy of nonprimitive square-zero matrices is established here.
